TransferNamespaceRequest.description: The namespace a repository is being transferred into.

namespace.description:
The destination namespace, as addressed on disk. A UUID where a control plane owns
namespaces, and the namespace's name where the server owns its own.

namespace_name.description:
What the destination namespace is called, where `namespace` addresses it by UUID instead.
Recorded as the repository's namespace hint, and refused when it is not a valid namespace
name. A server that owns its own namespaces takes the name from the `namespace` position and
ignores this.

PathHistoryPage.description:
One page of the commits that changed a file or directory, newest first. The history is not
counted, so the page reports whether a later one exists rather than how many there are.

A commit history response: a revision's history carries its totals, and a file or directory's
history reports whether a later page exists.

CommitSide.description:
Which side of a comparison a commit came from, mirroring the markers git's
`log --left-right base...head` prints.

WorkspaceView.description:
Used to send workspace state across the wire. The `Workspace`'s other fields (like
`LocalRepository`) would bloat the response and leak internal state.

CommitEntry.description:
Represents a file or directory entry at a specific commit.

`Hash` and `Eq` are based on the content hash field, so `HashSet<CommitEntry>`
deduplicates by file content. This is used during fetch and push to avoid
transferring the same content twice.

RepoNew.description: Only used between client and server for creating a new remote repository.

name.description:
The name of the repository. When cloned locally, this is the name of the directory.
This name uniquely identifies it in the namespace.

namespace.description:
The namespace that the repository lives in: dictates application-level repository ownership.
A namespace can be e.g. a user, a team, or an entire organization. Namespaces must be unique.

namespace_name.description:
What the namespace is called, where `namespace` addresses it by UUID instead. Recorded as a
hint beside the identity, ignored by a server that owns its own namespaces, and refused when
it is not a valid namespace name.

repo_name.description:
What the repository is called, where `name` addresses it by UUID instead. Recorded as a hint
beside the identity, ignored by a server that owns its own namespaces, and refused when it
is not a valid repository name.

repo_uuid.description:
The immutable UUID to address the new repo's storage by. Supplied by an external control
plane that owns repository identity; `None` leaves the choice to the server.

oneOf.description: Which storage backend the server should use for this repo (e.g. "local", "s3").

StorageKind.description: Storage backend kind. Serializes as `"local"` / `"s3"` on the wire and on disk.

MetadataEntry.description:
`deny_unknown_fields` is the discriminator for the untagged `EMetadataEntry` enum:
payloads with a `changes` field (i.e. `WorkspaceMetadataEntry`) fail to deserialize here
and fall through to the workspace variant.

VersionUploadStart.description: Where a file stands once its upload starts, in the response's `file` field.

oneOf.description: Send parts 1 through `num_parts` to `upload_id`, each `part_size` bytes but the last.

part_window.description:
How many consecutive parts the upload accepts at once, starting at the first part not
yet hashed. A part past them gets 429, so a client sending parts in order keeps at most
this many in flight.

oneOf.description:
The store already had the file, so it needs no parts, and it is staged at the destination,
if one was given.

NewCommitBody.description: NewCommitBody is used to parse the json into a Commit from the API

repo_uuid.description:
The immutable UUID this repo's storage is addressed by. `None` for a repository whose
identity backfill has not run.

ParsedResourceView.description: External (view) model that is returned to the client with fewer fields.

SummarizedStagedDirStats.description:
This is a representation of directories that are staged and we want a top level summary of counts
For example:
  annotations/
    train/
      annotations.csv
      one_shot.csv
      unstaged.csv
    test/
      annotations.csv

Would have:
    annotations/train/ -> num_staged: 2, total: 3
    annotations/test/ -> num_staged: 1, total: 1

Rolled up to:
    annotations/ -> num_staged: 3, total: 4

What the repository is called from now on, recorded as its name hint. Refused when it is not

A commit in a comparison, tagged with the side it came from. Every commit of a two-dot
comparison is on the head side; a three-dot comparison reports commits from both.

created_at.description: `None` for a workspace created before the server recorded creation time.

repo_uuid.description:
The immutable UUID this repo's storage is addressed by. `None` for a repository whose
identity backfill has not run.

put.description: Upload one part of a file. A part may arrive up to `part_window` parts from the earliest part not yet hashed, counting that part, and one further ahead is refused with 429 and Retry-After, as is a part sent again while its first copy is still being stored. Until the upload completes, a part sent again after it was stored is accepted and ignored. Once it completes, any part gets 404, as for an upload that was aborted, so a client that lost the response for the last part begins the upload again, which answers with no parts to send once the file is stored. Each part but the last is exactly the upload's part size. The response for the part that completes the file reports `completed: true`, once the file is verified against its hash and staged in the upload's workspace, if it has one.

parameters.description: The id the upload began with
parameters.name: upload_id

400.description: Part out of range, of the wrong length, or the file's bytes do not match its hash

404.description: Upload not found: it never began, was aborted, or already completed

429.description: Part arrived too far ahead of the parts before it, or an earlier copy of it is still being stored. Send it again after Retry-After

post.description: Begin uploading a large file in parts. A file may be at most 1 TiB, a provisional limit. The response's `file` is `awaiting_parts`, with the upload id, the size of every part but the last, the number of parts, and how many parts the upload accepts at once, starting at the first part not yet hashed. When the request gives a destination, a workspace and a path, the file is staged there once its last part arrives. When the store already has the file, `file` is `already_stored`: no parts are needed, and the file is staged at the destination, if one was given. A client whose upload completed without a response, or failed to stage, begins it again.
